reuse_policy: Controlled reuse after release checks; no permanent protected-code list. Use full title and version/date to interpret historical references to a reused code.

rules.title: Classify by process outcome
rules.text: Assign one code according to the primary business outcome. Use secondary business-area tags and cross-references for shared procedures. A D365 module, team, country or system alone does not determine the code.

rules.title: Create a guide only when needed
rules.text: Use a separate PG for a distinct trigger and outcome or a substantial standalone procedure. Keep related scenarios, screens and reports as topics where one coherent guide serves the reader. A family allocation does not require a guide at every number.

rules.title: Check and record allocations
rules.text: Check the master register, Hub library and working drafts before allocating. Record code, title, scope, owner, date, reason, status, predecessor and document links. Use an available code within the correct family; an empty-looking gap is not evidence of availability.

rules.title: Keep code and version separate
rules.text: Use NNN-Guide Title PG vX.Y.docx for working Word files and NNN-Guide Title PG.pdf for published PDFs. A title correction, revision, reviewer or approval status does not change the code. Do not renumber active guides merely to close gaps.

rules.title: Allow controlled reuse
rules.text: Former codes are not permanently blocked. Release a code when no active guide or draft uses it and maintained references to its former meaning are updated or explicitly resolved. Record the release date and owner, retain dated history, and allocate only within the current family. Do not reuse automatically because a file was renamed.

rules.title: Handle growth and shared work
rules.text: Define an unallocated family before assigning its first guide. Review capacity before extending into another block. Splits and mergers require predecessor and successor records. Never give two active guides the same code or duplicate a shared procedure under separate stream codes.
